prompt: Use average bond enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹: C–H 414, O=O 498, C=O 804, O–H 463) to estimate ΔH for $\text{CH}_4(g)+2\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{CO}_2(g)+2\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$.
markscheme:
Bonds broken $=4(414)+2(498)=2652$ kJ **(A1)**; bonds formed $=2(804)+4(463)=3460$ kJ **(A1)**

$\Delta H=2652-3460=-808\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)** — an estimate, since bond enthalpies are averages for gaseous species.

prompt: Given $\text{C}(s)+\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{CO}_2(g)$, $\Delta H=-394$ kJ and $\text{CO}(g)+\tfrac12\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{CO}_2(g)$, $\Delta H=-283$ kJ, calculate ΔH for $\text{C}(s)+\tfrac12\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{CO}(g)$.
markscheme:
Route: C → CO₂ directly equals C → CO → CO₂ **(M1)**: $\Delta H=-394-(-283)=-111$ kJ **(A1)**

Useful because this reaction cannot be measured directly (some CO₂ always forms).

concept: Standard enthalpies of formation and combustion
prompt: Define standard enthalpy of formation, and state the value for O₂(g), with a reason.
markscheme: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states under standard conditions **(A1)**; for O₂(g) it is zero, because it is already an element in its standard state **(R1)**

prompt: Calculate ΔH for $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8(g)+5\text{O}_2(g)\to3\text{CO}_2(g)+4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. ($\Delta H_f$ in kJ mol⁻¹: C₃H₈ −105, CO₂ −394, H₂O(l) −286)
Calculate ΔH for $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g)+\text{H}_2(g)\to\text{C}_2\text{H}_6(g)$ using $\Delta H_c$ (kJ mol⁻¹): C₂H₄ −1411, H₂ −286, C₂H₆ −1561.
markscheme:
With combustion data: $\Delta H=\sum\Delta H_c(\text{reactants})-\sum\Delta H_c(\text{products})$ **(M1)**

$=-1411-286-(-1561)=-136\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A2)**

**Common mistake:** using products minus reactants, as for formation data.

prompt: Use the data to calculate the lattice enthalpy of NaCl (kJ mol⁻¹): $\Delta H_f(\text{NaCl})=-411$; atomisation of Na $+107$; first IE of Na $+496$; $\tfrac12$ bond enthalpy Cl–Cl $+121$; electron affinity of Cl $-349$.
markscheme:
Lattice enthalpy (NaCl(s) → Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g)) $=-\Delta H_f+\Delta H_{at}(\text{Na})+IE+\tfrac12E(\text{Cl–Cl})+EA$ **(M1)(A1)**

$=411+107+496+121-349=+786\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A2)**
